fatal_errors: The proposed CoCrFeMnNi material is not a lightweight alloy and does not reconstruct the MgAlTiVFeCo ball-milled BCC powder system.
The intervention is an unconstrained mixture of compositional and processing changes rather than a controlled comparison of spark-plasma-sintering temperatures culminating at 1000 °C.
The grain-boundary mechanism conflicts with the target mechanism involving densification, uniformly distributed oxide barrier phases, passive-film formation, and diffusion-controlled oxidation.
Inconel 718 is the wrong baseline; the relevant controls are otherwise identical specimens sintered at lower temperatures.
The predicted percentage improvements and falsification thresholds are invented without supporting observations or cited evidence.
explanation: The response recognizes the desired property combination and includes NaCl corrosion testing, elevated-temperature oxidation, comparative measurements, and an upper-temperature failure boundary. However, it misses nearly every material-specific feature of the target: composition and powder state, the 1000 °C SPS intervention, lower-temperature controls, oxide barrier phases, passive-film behavior, biphasic parabolic oxidation, and the reported density, hardness, electrochemical, and oxidation-kinetic results. Its experiment also changes alloy chemistry and processing simultaneously, so it cannot isolate grain-boundary density as the causal mediator. With no supporting evidence and a scientifically overgeneralized claim that grain boundaries inhibit corrosion and oxidation, it is not a supported alternative hypothesis.
